gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SoundGuys' lab gave the soundcore Space 2 Pro a noise-cancelling score of 8.8/10, an average cut of over 88% of outside noise, which is above the 8.7/10 it gave both the Sony WH-1000XM6 and the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen).
standout_why: I compared against SoundGuys' 'best noise canceling headphones for work' page (cited, Adam Birney, 2026-10-22), SoundGuys' 'I lab-tested the best noise cancelling headphones' page (in the results, 2026-10-30) and SoundGuys' 'headphones with mic for conference calls' page (in the results, 2026-03-24). None of them mentions the Space 2 Pro, which was reviewed on 2026-11-09. None gives an ANC score out of 10 for the Sony or the Bose; the noise-cancelling pages show only overall ratings of 8.3 and 8.2. The conference-calls page says it has no isolation or mic measurements while its test rig is being rebuilt. None of them shows SoundGuys' reader mic-poll results either. I could not read the two cited RTINGS pages (the phone-calls list and the Bose vs Sony comparison): WebFetch returned only the site navigation, so I can't say whether they hold the same figures.
decides: Under one reviewer's lab method, the Space 2 Pro (which we list) cuts noise at least as well as the two $449-list flagships ChatGPT recommended. That backs it as the value pick for ANC plus calls. Measured battery favours Sony over Bose (37 h 14 min vs 27 h 12 min with ANC on, both SoundGuys). SoundGuys readers rated the Sony and Bose mics about the same: 51% and 53% voted Good or Excellent. For the boom-mic Jabra Evolve2 85, only 24% voted Good or Perfect. That reader poll alone does not justify recommending a boom headset over the consumer over-ears.
